title: The Eastern Tribes and the Altar

date.label: Undated Joshua eastern-tribes narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: East-bank tribes are commended and discharged (Joshua 22:1–9)
A large Jordan-region altar triggers western suspicion (Joshua 22:10–20)
Eastern group denies intention to use altar for sacrifices (Joshua 22:21–29)
The episode closes with restored agreement, without battle (Joshua 22:30–34)
The altar’s name and final verse have textual/translation difficulty (Joshua 22:34)
claims.evidence: KJV Joshua 22:34 (BibleGateway KJV); SIL Translation Insights & Perspectives, Joshua 22:34 (Bratcher & Newman, UBS Handbook on Joshua): the name of the altar is missing in the Hebrew, and a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac add 'witness' as a name — a scribal attempt to ease the difficulty of the Hebrew text.

connections.note: The earlier terms of the east-bank tribes’ participation explain their release.
Joshua 1:12–18 anticipates the eastern tribes’ obligation; Joshua 22:1–9 recounts their subsequent release.
Cult-centralization prescriptions contextualize accusation while chronology remains debated.
The witness pillar and heap share commemorative legal symbolism with the altar, but they are not the same event.
The Peor crisis is explicitly invoked within the accusers’ argument.
